headline: Reported Wellington IT breach exposes member data at about 50 credit unions, mostly in Ireland
summary: A reported cyberattack on IT provider Wellington IT has exposed sensitive member information belonging to about 50 credit unions. Most of them, reportedly about 40, are in Ireland. The incident shows the concentration risk that shared service providers create for regulated financial institutions.

headline: CISA adds actively exploited Puppet Enterprise RCE flaw CVE-2026-115731 to KEV
summary: Attackers are exploiting CVE-2026-115731, a critical remote code execution flaw in Perforce Puppet Enterprise. CISA added it to the KEV catalog and set a December 1, 2026 remediation deadline for US federal civilian agencies. Details of the attacks have not been made public.

summary: Versions 1.26.1 and 1.26.2 of Microsoft's official agent-framework package on PyPI were published on November 17, 2026 with code that steals cloud and CI/CD credentials. StepSecurity, OX Security and Socket detected the malicious releases.

summary: Socket reports that agent-framework versions 1.26.1 and 1.26.2 on PyPI were compromised. The malicious releases use .pth startup hooks to steal Azure, GitHub Actions and CI/CD credentials.

headline: N-able confirms intrusion into Mail Assure and Spam Experts hosted cloud server
summary: N-able says unknown attackers gained access to a server in its Mail Assure and Spam Experts hosted cloud. The company disabled management interfaces and APIs, which disrupted email security management in three regions. The investigation is still ongoing.

headline: European Commission internal HR systems hit by cyberattack
summary: A cyberattack has affected internal HR systems at the European Commission. Investigators are still checking whether sensitive data was accessed. The source gives no details on the method or who carried out the attack.

headline: European Commission confirms reportedly AI-driven cyberattack took some systems offline
summary: The European Commission has confirmed a cyberattack that targeted "individual systems" and took some of them offline. According to reports, the attackers used a tool called ARTEX, but the details have not been confirmed.

headline: Equinor investigates cyberattack affecting IT systems; production reportedly unaffected
summary: Norwegian oil and gas company Equinor is investigating a cyberattack that disrupted its IT systems. The company says production was not disrupted, but it has given no timeline for full recovery. Attribution and the attack type have not been disclosed.

headline: Norwegian energy firm Equinor hit by cyberattack disrupting IT applications
summary: Dutch outlet Security.NL reports that a cyberattack hit Equinor and affected its use of IT applications. Further details on scope and cause were not given in the excerpt.

headline: Apache Roller unauthenticated deserialization RCE reported under active exploitation
summary: The Apache Software Foundation reports active exploitation of CVE-2026-129448 (CVSS 9.8) in Apache Roller, a Java-based blogging platform. The flaw is an unauthenticated deserialization issue in the XML-RPC endpoint that can lead to remote code execution. Scale of exploitation and affected victims were not detailed.

headline: CERT-EU urges rapid NGINX patching after F5 discloses five unauthenticated RCE flaws
summary: CERT-EU Security Advisories: CERT-EU flagged F5's 18 November 2026 advisory on five NGINX vulnerabilities that let an unauthenticated remote attacker run code with worker-process privileges. Researchers have demonstrated CVE-2026-123007, but no exploitation in the wild has been reported. CERT-EU recommends patching quickly, starting with internet-facing systems. The Hacker News: CVE-2026-123007 affects NGINX's HTTP/2 support in every version since 1.9.5 (2015) and can let an unauthenticated attacker run code on servers with HTTP/2 enabled. Fixed versions 1.31.9 and 1.30.7 are available. Qualys Vulnerabilities and Threat Research: Five nginx vulnerabilities called NGINX2Root were disclosed on 18 November 2026. The lead flaw, CVE-2026-123007, is a memory corruption bug in nginx's HTTP/2 handling that F5 rates 9.2 under CVSS v4.0 and 8.1 under CVSS v3.1. An attacker without credentials can crash nginx worker processes; the source does not report exploitation in the wild.

headline: Researchers publish five NGINX exploits, including an HTTP/2-plus-kernel chain for full host takeover
summary: Researchers released five NGINX exploits. One chains an HTTP/2 bug with a kernel flaw to take over the server running NGINX. The report does not mention exploitation in the wild, but public exploits raise patching urgency.

headline: PHP2Shell flaws exploited against internet-exposed PAN-OS management interfaces
summary: Palo Alto Networks confirmed on October 28 that attackers were exploiting two PHP vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, against PAN-OS management interfaces exposed to the internet. Both flaws allow remote code execution without authentication. The article argues that firewall management planes carry ordinary web-application risk.

headline: F5 patches five critical NGINX2Root flaws as public PoC exploits appear
summary: F5 released patches for five vulnerabilities, called NGINX2Root, that could let remote, unauthenticated attackers run arbitrary code. Proof-of-concept exploits have been published. The source does not report exploitation in the wild.

headline: Five critical NGINX vulnerabilities could allow unauthenticated remote code execution
summary: Researchers disclosed five critical vulnerabilities in the NGINX web server. Unauthenticated attackers could use them to execute code remotely and potentially take control of affected servers. No exploitation is reported in the source.

headline: PHP Foundation schedules security release fixing multiple critical vulnerabilities
summary: The PHP Foundation announced a planned security update that addresses several critical vulnerabilities in the PHP language. The source gives no CVE details or reports of exploitation.

headline: PHP pre-announces security releases fixing critical flaws in all supported versions on November 19
summary: PHP maintainers say a security release scheduled for November 19, 2026 will fix critical vulnerabilities in all supported PHP versions. No CVE details or reports of exploitation were included in the announcement.

headline: Java4Shell exploitation attempts observed as Cisco, Elastic, Red Hat and Siemens issue advisories
summary: GreyNoise, watchTowr and Cloudflare report probing and exploitation attempts against the Java vulnerability dubbed Java4Shell. Cisco, Elastic, Red Hat and Siemens have published impact advisories. The source describes attempts and does not confirm successful compromises.

headline: Rakuten Securities discloses data breach potentially affecting 15 million customers
summary: Rakuten Securities, a broker based in Japan, has disclosed a data breach involving customer account details. The company says up to 15 million customers could be affected. The source gives no details on how the breach happened.

headline: PHP prepares critical updates for session upload progress RCE flaw CVE-2026-115560
summary: PHP is preparing critical security updates for CVE-2026-115560, a remote code execution flaw in the session upload progress feature. The flaw was publicly disclosed two days after the PHP2Shell patches were released. The source does not report any exploitation.

headline: COLD RELIC (Star Blizzard) poses as staff of breached organizations to phish new targets
summary: Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) reports that COLD RELIC, also known as Star Blizzard, Callisto and Gossamer Bear, impersonates employees of organizations it has already breached to phish new victims. The US Department of Justice has assessed that the group operates within Russia's FSB. Its targets are government officials, defense contractors and NGOs in Europe and North America.

headline: Dutch NCSC warns it expects large-scale exploitation of an NGINX vulnerability
summary: The Dutch National Cyber Security Centre says it is preparing for large-scale abuse of a vulnerability in NGINX. The source gives no CVE or confirmed successful compromises.

headline: Dutch police link violent incidents in Amsterdam and The Hague to Revolut data breach
summary: Dutch police say several violent incidents in Amsterdam and The Hague are linked to a data breach at Revolut. The source excerpt gives no details on how the leaked data was used, which suggests customer data exposure is causing physical-world harm.

headline: NGINX HTTP/2 heap overflow could allow worker crash or code execution (CVE-2026-123007)
summary: Undisclosed HTTP/2 traffic can push NGINX's flow-control window past its limit, causing a heap buffer overflow. The usual result is a worker crash. Remote code execution may be possible if ASLR is disabled or bypassed. No exploitation has been reported.

headline: Censys publishes a test and reproductions for the nginx2root vulnerabilities in nginx
summary: Censys published a simple test for the HTTP/2 flaw in the nginx2root set and reproduced three use-after-free bugs. The five flaws, disclosed by Xint, each corrupt memory in an nginx worker process and depend on specific features: HTTP/2, reverse proxying over HTTP/2 or HTTP/3, runtime DNS resolution with subrequests, or mail proxy authentication. The source does not report exploitation in the wild.

headline: NGINX HTTP/3 use-after-free can restart workers and may allow code execution
summary: NGINX Plus and NGINX Open Source configurations that use HTTP/3 contain a use-after-free that a remote unauthenticated attacker can trigger to restart worker processes. Exploitation depends on conditions outside the attacker's control, and code execution is possible if ASLR is disabled or bypassed. Amazon Linux affected status and patch availability are not established.

summary: CISA has added four actively exploited vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. They affect Synology DiskStation Manager, BerriAI LiteLLM, Apache Axis and REDCap, and CISA links the activity to ransomware, cryptomining and LLMjacking. The CVE identifiers were not included in the supplied text.

headline: Cisco Expressway vulnerability exploited shortly after public PoC release
summary: Attackers reportedly compromised clustered Cisco Expressway devices at an organization in Russia soon after a proof-of-concept exploit became public. They also staged tooling for lateral movement. The source does not name the CVE or the attacker.

headline: NGINX2Root: five nginx flaws include an unauthenticated HTTP/2 memory corruption bug
summary: Researchers disclosed five nginx vulnerabilities under the name NGINX2Root. The main flaw, CVE-2026-123007, is HTTP/2 memory corruption that lets an unauthenticated attacker crash worker processes. Researchers demonstrated code execution with worker privileges, but the source does not report exploitation in the wild.

headline: "Java4Shell" memory corruption flaw in OpenJDK runtime may allow unauthenticated system takeover
summary: A memory corruption vulnerability nicknamed Java4Shell was found in the OpenJDK runtime with the help of AI. It could allow unauthenticated attackers to take over affected systems. The source does not report a CVE or any in-the-wild exploitation.

headline: Critical Apache Roller and Axis flaws exploited, including attacks on Confluence Data Center
summary: Attackers are using an Apache Axis vulnerability to target Atlassian Confluence Data Center. Apache has also warned of attacks against Roller. The source does not give CVE identifiers.

summary: SANS ISC explained why it has not raised its Infocon level again after the earlier php2shell alert. It points to several recent events: a major Microsoft 365 outage, a critical Java vulnerability and a critical NGINX vulnerability disclosed this week. The source does not give CVE identifiers or say whether either flaw is being exploited.

headline: Critical Java vulnerability could affect many popular applications, though exploitation is hard
summary: Researchers have disclosed a critical Java vulnerability that could have wide downstream effects on applications built on Java. They cautioned that exploitation would not be easy. The source gives no CVE identifier or reports of active exploitation.

headline: F5 discloses six critical BIG-IP flaws enabling unauthenticated TMM crashes in specific configurations
summary: F5 disclosed six critical BIG-IP vulnerabilities that let an unauthenticated attacker crash the Traffic Management Microkernel and disrupt traffic until it restarts. Each flaw needs a specific virtual server configuration involving certain iRule commands or APM policy agents, and the reporting says remote code execution may be possible. The source does not report any exploitation.

headline: Researcher publishes low-privilege RCE proofs of concept for PostgreSQL, MySQL, ClickHouse and Oracle
summary: A researcher has published proofs of concept showing that low-privilege database accounts can run code on the database server. The exploits reach memory-corruption bugs in database engine code through ordinary SQL. They target PostgreSQL, MySQL and ClickHouse, with a separate exploit chain for Oracle, and the source does not report any exploitation in the wild.

headline: TfL warns 265,000 Oyster Photocard customers their personal data may have been exposed
summary: Transport for London is warning about 265,000 photocard customers that their personal data may have been exposed. The incident came to light after emails were sent to Oyster Photocard customers from TfL's own systems.

headline: Drupal patches critical RCE flaw and warns exploits may appear quickly
summary: The Drupal Security Team has fixed a critical remote code execution flaw that could let attackers take over sites. It warned that exploits may appear soon, but the source reports no exploitation yet.

headline: Drupal warns of critical flaw allowing unauthenticated website takeover
summary: Drupal's maintainers have warned about a critical vulnerability that could let unauthenticated attackers take over sites built on the CMS. The source does not mention a CVE identifier or any active exploitation.

headline: Ruby patches seven regex and string memory-safety flaws, five with PoC remote code execution
summary: Ruby maintainers fixed seven memory-safety bugs in the regex engine and in string case-conversion code. They say proof-of-concept exploits show some of the flaws can lead to code execution through crafted input. No in-the-wild exploitation is reported.

headline: Splunk fixes about 140 vulnerabilities across three core products, including critical flaws
summary: Splunk released security updates for nearly 140 vulnerabilities across three core products. Some are critical or high severity and could allow authentication bypass, remote code execution or privilege escalation. The source does not report any exploitation.

headline: NGINX HTTP/2 proxy use-after-free enables denial of service and possible code execution (CVE-2026-123633)
summary: CVE-2026-123633 affects NGINX Plus and NGINX Open Source when they use HTTP/2 for client connections and proxy requests to a backend. A crafted request can trigger a use-after-free in a worker process that is running low on worker_connections. This causes denial of service, and code execution is possible if ASLR is disabled or can be bypassed. No exploitation has been reported in the source.

headline: NGINX proxy use-after-free with SSI or mirror subrequests may allow RCE
summary: The flaw affects NGINX proxy setups whose proxied server name uses variables, combined with SSI or mirror subrequests. In that setup, a crafted request can cause a use-after-free that crashes workers or corrupts memory. Code execution is possible only if ASLR is disabled or bypassed, and no exploitation is reported.

headline: SonicWall Gen 6 firewalls reach end of support; vendor urges immediate replacement
summary: All SonicWall Gen 6 and Gen 6.5 appliances running SonicOS 6.x have reached end of support and will get no further patches, whatever the severity. SonicWall calls internet-facing units a high-risk exposure and advises taking them off the network edge immediately.

headline: Siemens RUGGEDCOM ROX II web CLI vulnerable to CSRF device takeover
summary: An updated CISA advisory covers a CSRF flaw (CVE-2020-28398, CVSS 8.8) in the web CLI of RUGGEDCOM ROX II industrial network devices. Tricking a logged-in administrator into clicking a malicious link could let an attacker read or change the device configuration. V2.16.0 fixes the flaw; the CVSS vector notes proof-of-concept exploit maturity.

headline: CISA updates advisory on Danfoss AK-SM 8xxA flaws enabling authentication bypass and RCE
summary: CISA has updated ICS advisory ICSA-25-140-03, which covers three vulnerabilities in Danfoss AK-SM 8xxA system managers. They include a predictable, datetime-based password that allows authentication bypass (CVSS 8.2), a post-authentication command injection, and a denial-of-service issue. Danfoss has fixed them in releases R4.2 and R4.3.1; the advisory does not report exploitation.

headline: Synology warns of critical NAS flaw allowing remote file access
summary: Synology has disclosed a critical vulnerability that could let a remote attacker access files stored on its NAS systems. The source does not report exploitation, a CVE identifier or a public PoC.

headline: NGINX mail proxy use-after-free may allow denial of service or code execution
summary: When NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source runs as a mail proxy, unauthenticated traffic can trigger a use-after-free in a worker process. This can crash the worker, and code execution is possible if ASLR is disabled or bypassed. Amazon Linux affected status and patch availability are not established.

headline: CISA updates advisory on Geutebrück IP camera firmware flaws allowing unauthenticated access and RCE
summary: CISA has updated its advisory on Geutebrück G-Cam E2 and G-Code cameras and encoders, which use firmware from UDP Technology. The flaws include unauthenticated access to sensitive files (CVE-2021-33543, CVSS 9.8) and authenticated command injection and buffer overflows that could allow remote code execution. Firmware 1.12.14.7 fixes the issues.

headline: Ukraine arrests four suspected ransomware members accused of $40M extortion
summary: Ukrainian authorities arrested four suspected members of an international ransomware network. The group is accused of extorting more than $40 million from companies worldwide, including US oil and healthcare firms.

headline: Ukrainian police and FBI detain four members of ransomware gang that posed as IT support
summary: Ukraine's National Police say four key members of a ransomware group were detained after an investigation run with the FBI for more than two years. Police say the group extorted more than $40.5 million from at least 28 companies. It got into corporate networks by phoning targets and posing as IT support staff.

headline: CISA republishes Geutebrück G-Cam advisory for critical authentication bypass and RCE flaws
summary: CISA has reissued advisory ICSA-17-045-02 (version 2) for two flaws in Geutebrück G-Cam/EFD-2250 IP camera firmware version 1.11.0.12. The flaws are an authentication bypass and a command injection, each rated CVSS 9.8. Both are remotely exploitable and could give an attacker root-level code execution. The vendor has released a patch, and no exploitation has been reported.

headline: CISA republishes advisory on Geutebrück G-Cam/G-Code root command injection (CVE-2020-16205)
summary: CISA has released version 2 of an older advisory for Geutebrück G-Cam and G-Code IP camera firmware. On firmware 1.12.0.25 and earlier, an authenticated remote user with high privileges can run commands as root through a specially crafted URL (CVSS 7.2). Geutebrück recommends updating to firmware 1.12.0.27. The advisory reports no exploitation.

headline: Ukraine and FBI arrest four suspected members of a ransomware gang linked to $40.5M in ransoms
summary: Working with the FBI, Ukrainian authorities arrested four suspected members of an international ransomware group. The group is linked to more than $40.5 million in ransom payments from at least 28 companies worldwide. The source does not name the gang.

headline: CISA republishes Hitachi Energy MicroSCADA SYS600 advisory on legacy ActiveX code execution flaw
summary: CISA has issued version 2 of a Hitachi Energy advisory for MicroSCADA Pro/X SYS600. The legacy ActiveBar ActiveX control (CVE-2011-1207, CVSS 6.7) could allow arbitrary code execution. Hitachi Energy recommends upgrading to SYS600 10.2 or applying its general mitigations. The advisory does not report any exploitation.

headline: Hitachi Energy AFS, AFR and AFF network devices affected by libexpat flaws; AFS65x gets no fix
summary: CISA has updated its advisory on libexpat use-after-free flaws in Hitachi Energy's AFS, AFR and AFF industrial network switches and routers. Exploitation could expose sensitive information or cause a denial of service. Some product lines have firmware updates now or coming, but the end-of-life AFS65x will only get mitigations.

headline: NGINX TLSv1.3 flaw can trigger worker infinite loop and denial of service
summary: A remote, unauthenticated attacker can send a crafted TLS connection that puts NGINX workers into an infinite loop while they read the request body. This affects SSL listeners with TLSv1.3 enabled. Stuck workers stop handling connections, which causes a denial of service; no exploitation is reported.

headline: NGINX ssl_preread flaw lets crafted ClientHello bypass stream routing segmentation
summary: An unauthenticated crafted ClientHello can forge ngx_stream_ssl_preread_module variables and change which virtual server NGINX selects. An attacker could then reach internal or privileged backends and possibly sensitive data. No exploitation is reported.

headline: ReversingLabs expands analysis of Turla CerealLoader targeting Exchange servers
summary: Building on an earlier ESET disclosure, ReversingLabs connected CerealLoader samples that appear under different vendor names and file variants, and it reports 12 Exchange-related loaders. The researchers also found more possible loaders and tested where common detection approaches miss them. The source does not name specific victims or new exploited CVEs.

headline: Schneider Electric Enerlin'X IFE/eIFE flaws allow denial of service on circuit-breaker interfaces
summary: An updated CISA advisory covers three input-validation flaws in Schneider Electric Enerlin'X IFE and eIFE Ethernet interfaces for circuit breakers. Malformed IPv6, ICMPv6 or IEC 61850-MMS packets can disrupt the device's network services, and recovery may need a manual reboot. Firmware 004.010.000 fixes the MMS issue; the IPv6 and ICMPv6 issues rely on mitigations such as segmentation.

headline: Siemens SICAM A8000 CP-8031/CP-8050 flaw allows firmware decryption via physical SPI bus access
summary: CISA has republished a Siemens advisory, now at version 3, for CVE-2024-53832 in SICAM A8000 CPCI85 modules. If an attacker can physically reach the unencrypted SPI bus, they can capture the secure element password and then use the element to decrypt firmware update files. Fixing it requires both new firmware (V05.30 or later) and new hardware.

headline: Schneider Electric Vijeo Designer privilege escalation flaw now fixed in EcoStruxure Machine Expert
summary: CISA has updated its advisory for CVE-2024-8306 (CVSS 7.8), an improper privilege management flaw in Vijeo Designer HMI configuration software. A logged-in user without admin rights could gain higher privileges by tampering with binaries. Fixes are now available in Vijeo Designer V6.3 SP1 and in EcoStruxure Machine Expert v2.3.

headline: JTEKT Kostac PLC programming software has project-file flaws that could allow code execution
summary: CISA has updated its advisory on three flaws in JTEKT ELECTRONICS Kostac PLC programming software up to version 1.6.9.0: two out-of-bounds reads and one use-after-free (each CVSS 7.8). Opening a crafted project file could disclose information or run code. Version 1.6.10.0 fixes the flaws and adds tamper protection for project files.

headline: AttackIQ research maps how Iranian state groups hand off network access for destructive attacks
summary: AttackIQ looked at 20 Iranian state-sponsored threat groups. It describes how espionage, ransomware and hacktivist activity overlap, and how one group can pass network access to another that then carries out a destructive attack. The source names no specific campaigns or victims.

headline: ansible-core path traversal lets malicious Galaxy collections overwrite directories
summary: A flaw in ansible-galaxy collection install takes the install path from collection metadata without validating it. A crafted collection can delete a directory the user can write to and place attacker files outside the collections path. The record does not confirm whether Amazon Linux is affected or patched.

headline: NGINX stream virtual server flaw can bypass client certificate verification
summary: A vulnerability in NGINX Plus and NGINX Open Source lets a remote attacker bypass client certificate checks when ssl_verify_client is on in a non-default stream virtual server. It affects only the data plane. The Amazon Linux record does not confirm whether Amazon Linux is affected or whether a patch is available.

headline: MITRE says 87% of recent CVE records carry inaccurate publication timestamps
summary: MITRE has acknowledged that most of its recent CVE records have incorrect publication timestamps. It plans to retire the legacy system behind the problem in 2027. This can distort patch-SLA metrics and vulnerability-feed processing that rely on these dates.

headline: NGINX worker crash flaw in try_files/alias with map variable configurations (CVE-2026-125283)
summary: CVE-2026-125283 affects NGINX Plus and NGINX Open Source. In certain configurations that combine try_files, alias and map-variable regex captures, a worker process can hit a segmentation fault, which allows denial of service. The flaw is in the data plane only. The source record does not confirm whether Amazon Linux is affected or whether a patch is available.

headline: US Homeland Security Task Force launches Threat Disruption Center to intercept scam proceeds
summary: The US Homeland Security Task Force has set up a Threat Disruption Center within its National Coordination Center. The center will work with private firms to stop victims' money before it reaches foreign scam, cybercrime and sextortion networks. Investigators get tools to triage victim complaints and map the criminal groups behind them.

headline: Officials link tech outages to rushed patching of AI-discovered vulnerabilities, not cyberattacks
summary: Reporting points to growing agreement that recent tech outages were driven by patching of vulnerabilities found with AI. Trump administration officials said cyberattacks were not directly to blame. The source does not name which outages or vendors were involved.

headline: Siemens Teamcenter Visualization WRL file-parsing flaws could enable code execution
summary: An updated CISA advisory lists many memory-corruption flaws in Siemens Teamcenter Visualization that are triggered by crafted WRL files. Most are rated CVSS 7.8 and require a user to open a malicious file. Siemens has released fixed versions.

headline: NGINX stream SSL configuration flaw allows workers to be terminated remotely
summary: An abbreviated SSL handshake can terminate NGINX worker processes when dynamic certificate loading in ngx_stream_ssl_module is combined with proxy_protocol v2 in ngx_stream_proxy_module. This can cause denial of service. Amazon Linux affected status and patch availability are not established.

headline: CISA re-issues LAquis SCADA advisory listing multiple RCE, hard-coded credential and auth bypass flaws
summary: CISA has released version 2 of a 2019 advisory covering 11 vulnerabilities in LAquis SCADA 4.1.0.3870. The flaws include file-parsing bugs that can lead to code execution, hard-coded credentials, path traversal and an authentication bypass. CVSS scores reach 7.8, and the fix is version 4.1.0.4150.

headline: CISA re-issues LAquis SCADA advisory on ELS file buffer overflow (CVE-2019-6536)
summary: CISA has released version 2 of a 2019 advisory for LCDS LAquis SCADA 4.1.0.4150. Opening a crafted ELS file can trigger an out-of-bounds write and code execution (CVSS 7.8). The vendor recommends upgrading to version 4.3.1.71.

headline: CNIL fines French company €5 million for storing passwords in plaintext
summary: CNIL, France's data protection regulator, fined a French company €5 million for storing passwords in plaintext. The source does not name the company or its sector.

headline: ansible-galaxy role install path traversal lets malicious roles write files outside role directory
summary: ansible-galaxy does not check role names taken from meta/requirements.yml. A malicious role or one of its transitive dependencies can write files outside the roles directory. With --force, it can also replace existing role directories. Impact is limited to the invoking user's permissions and requires installing attacker-influenced content.

headline: Arriva investigates possible data leak in Xbike bike-share app
summary: Arriva is investigating a possible data leak involving the Xbike bike-share app. The app has been taken offline as a precaution. It is not yet confirmed what data, if any, was exposed.

headline: Microsoft confirms app install and launch problems after this month's Windows 11 hotpatch
summary: Microsoft confirmed that this month's Windows 11 hotpatch can cause installation and launch problems for Office and third-party applications. Microsoft has published a workaround.

headline: DHS plans to seek earlier industry disclosure of major patches after recent tech disruptions
summary: Officials reviewed a recent run of tech disruptions in House Homeland Security testimony. DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin said the administration will ask companies to share more information about major patches before they take effect. No binding requirement was described.

headline: rsyslog imuxsock stack buffer underwrite with UsePIDFromSystem enabled (CVE-2026-129832)
summary: A flaw in rsyslog's imuxsock module causes a one-byte stack buffer underwrite when it handles a message with an empty TAG while UsePIDFromSystem is enabled. Only that non-default configuration is affected. The Amazon Linux record does not confirm affected status or patch availability, and no exploitation has been reported.

headline: Russian state-backed group Cold Relic reuses stolen cloud data to target new victims
summary: Dark Reading reports that the Russian state-sponsored group Cold Relic takes data stolen in one cloud breach and uses it to target other organisations. The group relies on convincing impersonation and social engineering. The source names no specific victims, sectors or countries.

headline: rsyslog out-of-bounds read crashes rsyslogd on crafted timestamps
summary: rsyslogd can crash with an out-of-bounds read when a template formats a crafted low-year timestamp as a weekday name. The result is a possible logging denial of service. The record does not confirm whether Amazon Linux is affected or patched.

headline: rsyslog imdtls flaw allows listener stall and permitted-peer check bypass (CVE-2026-129834)
summary: A flaw in rsyslog's imdtls DTLS input module can stall the listener and bypass permitted-peer checks during DTLS sessions. This could allow denial of service or unauthorised log injection. The record gives few details and does not confirm affected status or patch availability.

headline: rsyslog imdtls flaw can stall the listener and bypass permitted-peer checks
summary: A vulnerability in the imdtls DTLS input module can stall its listener and bypass permitted-peer checks during DTLS sessions. The record gives few details, and Amazon Linux affected status is not established.

headline: CISA republishes LAquis SCADA advisory covering multiple code execution flaws fixed in 4.1.0.4114
summary: CISA has reissued advisory ICSA-18-289-01 (version 2) for LCDS LAquis SCADA. It covers six 2018 flaws, including out-of-bounds reads, stack overflows and path traversal, with CVSS scores between 5.3 and 7.8 that could allow code execution or crashes. The vendor fix is version 4.1.0.4114. The advisory does not report any exploitation.

headline: Siemens COMOS XXE flaws could expose files on engineering systems
summary: An updated CISA advisory describes two XXE flaws in Siemens COMOS plant-engineering software. They could let an attacker pull files from the user's system or network shares through crafted configuration files or an injected interface channel. Fixes are available for some versions; others rely on mitigations.

headline: Siemens JT Open, JT Utilities and Parasolid flaws allow code execution via malicious JT files
summary: CISA has republished a Siemens advisory on out-of-bounds read flaws that are triggered when parsing JT files. A user who opens a crafted file could have arbitrary code run on their machine. Siemens has released updated versions of JT Open, JT Utilities and Parasolid.

headline: virglrenderer GBM buffer transfer flaw could allow guest VM memory corruption or escape (CVE-2026-130507)
summary: virglrenderer does not properly validate guest-supplied transfer parameters for GBM-backed resources. A malicious guest with 3D acceleration enabled could read or write host renderer memory out of bounds, leading to denial of service or potentially a VM escape. Only configurations with GBM buffer allocation enabled are affected.

headline: virglrenderer flaw lets malicious guest VM write out of bounds on host via crafted shaders (CVE-2026-130506)
summary: A malicious guest VM with virtio-gpu OpenGL acceleration enabled can send crafted linked shaders that cause an out-of-bounds write in virglrenderer on the host. At minimum this crashes the host renderer process, and further impact may be possible. Affected status on Amazon Linux is not established.

headline: EV charging app Chargemap leaks user personal data and password hashes
summary: Chargemap, an app for finding EV charging stations, has exposed users' personal information and password hashes. The source does not give the scale or the cause.

headline: Siemens Software Center DLL hijacking flaws allow local privilege escalation
summary: CISA has republished a Siemens advisory on DLL hijacking flaws in Siemens Software Center, including one in the bundled Qt library. A local attacker could run code with elevated privileges. Siemens Software Center V3.0 fixes the issues.

headline: US charges Russian national with surveilling defense-tech company employees for Moscow
summary: US prosecutors have charged a Russian national with acting as an agent of Moscow. He was allegedly recruited through Telegram to run surveillance on employees of a defense technology company, reportedly Palantir. The case shows that hostile intelligence services are targeting defense-sector staff, not only their systems.

headline: rsyslog imuxsock out-of-bounds write via local crafted messages (CVE-2026-129829)
summary: The rsyslog imuxsock parser can write past a message buffer when it rewrites timestamps. A local sender can trigger this with a malformed PRI field and a short timestamp. Code review confirms the out-of-bounds write. A reliable crash in ordinary builds has not been demonstrated.

headline: CISA re-issues Geutebrück E2 camera advisory on DDNS root command injection (CVE-2018-19007)
summary: CISA has released version 2 of a 2018 advisory for Geutebrück E2 series IP cameras. A privileged attacker can inject OS commands as root through the DDNS configuration (CVSS 7.2). Firmware 1.12.0.25 fixes the issue.

headline: CISA re-issues Geutebrück IP camera advisory covering root RCE and stored XSS flaws
summary: CISA has released version 2 of a 2019 advisory for Geutebrück G-Cam and G-Code cameras on firmware 1.12.0.25 and earlier. It covers two root command-injection flaws (CVE-2019-10956 and CVE-2019-10958, CVSS 7.2) and a stored XSS flaw (CVE-2019-10957). All three require authenticated access. Firmware 1.12.13.2 or later fixes them.

headline: NVIDIA investigates breach claim after Gentlemen ransomware group lists it on leak site
summary: BleepingComputer: NVIDIA says it is investigating after the Gentlemen ransomware group added the company to its dark web leak site. No breach has been confirmed, and no details of stolen data have been verified. Security.NL: The claim has not been verified.

headline: rsyslog imdtls flaw may stall the listener and bypass permitted-peer checks (CVE-2026-129836)
summary: CVE-2026-129836 describes a flaw in the imdtls module, which appears to be rsyslog's DTLS input module. During DTLS sessions, the flaw can stall the listener and bypass permitted-peer checks. The source gives few details and does not confirm whether Amazon Linux is affected.

headline: rsyslog mmanon stack buffer overflow when anonymizing IPv4-in-IPv6 text (CVE-2026-129833)
summary: CVE-2026-129833 is a stack buffer overflow in the mmanon module, which appears to be rsyslog's IP-anonymization module. It is triggered when the module processes embedded IPv4-in-IPv6 address text. The source gives few details and does not confirm whether Amazon Linux is affected.

headline: CISA updates advisory on Johnson Controls victor and C•CURE web client flaw allowing file deletion
summary: CISA has updated its advisory on the American Dynamics victor Web Client and Software House C•CURE Web Client, which are physical access-control software. A missing authorization check (CVE-2020-9048, CVSS 7.1) lets an unauthenticated attacker on an adjacent network delete arbitrary files or cause denial of service. Johnson Controls has released updates.

headline: libfontenc heap out-of-bounds write could allow local privilege escalation (CVE-2026-109908)
summary: CVE-2026-109908 is a heap out-of-bounds write in libfontenc versions before 1.1.10, caused by weak bounds checking when the library parses encoding files. Where the X server runs as root, a low-privileged local user could potentially escalate privileges. The source does not confirm whether Amazon Linux is affected.

headline: Dutch data protection authority warns of serious privacy risks from camera glasses
summary: The Dutch data protection authority (Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens) has warned the public about camera-equipped smart glasses. It cites serious privacy risks for both wearers and bystanders.

headline: libXfont PCF font parsing heap over-read fixed in version 2.0.10 (CVE-2026-109909)
summary: libXfont versions before 2.0.10 do not properly validate integer values when parsing PCF font files, which can cause an out-of-bounds heap read. Loading a malicious PCF font could leak process memory or crash the X server or application.

headline: ReversingLabs outlines detection strategies for ARTEX malware and related forks
summary: ReversingLabs published threat research on detecting ARTEX and its related forks. The source gives only a title, so it does not describe the malware's capabilities, targets or detection logic.

headline: Microsoft tests Lockdown Mode in Edge to reduce browser attack surface
summary: Microsoft is testing a Lockdown Mode for Edge that it says could help prevent browser-based attacks. The source gives only a short description of the feature.

headline: Coinbase blocks $4.7M in crypto transfers to scam using Elon Musk deepfake livestream
summary: Coinbase says it blocked $4.7 million in cryptocurrency transfers to scammers. The scam promoted a fake giveaway using an AI-generated deepfake of Elon Musk during a Tesla livestream that drew more than 500,000 viewers.

headline: Nvidia says it found no sign of compromise after Gentlemen ransomware listed it as a victim
summary: The Gentlemen ransomware group has named Nvidia as a victim on its leak site. Nvidia says it has found no indication that its systems were compromised, so the claim is unverified.

headline: Bipartisan senators urge White House to launch national effort on defensive AI cyber systems
summary: Two senators, one from each party, asked the White House to start a national effort against AI-enabled cyber threats, citing recent AI-related security incidents. This is a policy proposal, not binding regulation.

headline: Dashlane survey finds a fifth of UK employees share passwords with AI tools
summary: A Dashlane survey reports that about one in five UK workers have shared passwords with AI tools. Respondents also report giving these tools access to sensitive data, which raises governance concerns for enterprises.

headline: Senate committee advances FCC nominee while several bipartisan cyber bills stall
summary: Senate Republicans moved an FCC nominee forward. If confirmed, the nominee would give Republicans a 3-1 majority on the commission. Several bipartisan cyber bills are in limbo because Democrats did not attend the markup hearing.

headline: Vendor article: deepfakes and helpdesk impersonation call for stronger identity verification
summary: In a vendor-sponsored piece, Specops Software reviews social engineering attacks that use deepfakes, helpdesk impersonation and fake IT support requests to gain access. It argues for stronger identity checks at the helpdesk.

headline: Commentary: governance gaps as enterprises adopt open-weight AI models
summary: Organizations are adopting open-weight AI models for lower cost, more privacy and more control. The commentary argues that many are not handling the governance risks that come with these models. It offers guidance on closing those gaps.

headline: CISA republishes LAquis SCADA advisory for exception handler overflow CVE-2018-5463
summary: CISA has reissued advisory ICSA-18-095-03 (version 2) for a structured exception handler overflow in LAquis SCADA version 4.1.0.3391 and earlier. The flaw requires local access and is rated CVSS 7.0. It could crash the system or allow code execution. Version 4.1.0.3774 fixes the issue.

headline: CISA republishes LAquis SCADA improper access control advisory CVE-2017-6016
summary: CISA has reissued advisory ICSA-17-075-01 (version 2) for an improper access control flaw in LAquis SCADA. Builds of version 4.1 and earlier released before January 20, 2017 are affected. An authenticated user could modify application files to escalate privileges; the flaw is rated CVSS 7.3. The vendor has published an update.

headline: CISA republishes LAquis SCADA path traversal advisory CVE-2017-6020
summary: CISA has reissued advisory ICSA-17-082-01 (version 2) for a remotely exploitable path traversal flaw in LAquis SCADA versions before 4.1.0.3237. The flaw is rated CVSS 5.3 and could expose files to an attacker. The vendor fixed it in version 4.1.0.3237.

headline: Survey: SecOps leaders are reshaping the L1 analyst role as AI agent use in SOCs grows
summary: A survey reports that 74% of security leaders are already deploying AI agents in their SOCs. Many are redesigning the tier-1 (L1) analyst role as a result.

headline: Holiday-season bot fraud and social engineering span weeks beyond Black Friday
summary: An opinion piece argues that bot-driven fraud and holiday-themed social engineering run for many weeks, not just around Black Friday. It says this puts pressure on security teams and small businesses.

headline: rsyslog imuxsock short-timestamp parsing flaw allows one-byte over-read (CVE-2026-129830)
summary: A record in the Amazon Linux CVE index describes an rsyslog imuxsock flaw. When the system timestamp and its special parser are in use, a local sender with write access to the imuxsock socket can make the TAG parser read one byte past the message buffer. The index does not say whether Amazon Linux is affected or whether a patch is available.

headline: rsyslog imuxsock trusted-property field injection can spoof sender identity (CVE-2026-129838)
summary: When rsyslog's imuxsock adds plain trusted-property annotations to messages, a local process can inject extra fields through its process name or executable path. Systems that consume the logs downstream might then treat values controlled by the attacker as sender identity that came from the kernel. The index does not establish whether Amazon Linux is affected or patched.

headline: US bankruptcy judge approves Google's $10M purchase of defunct Spirit Airlines' data
summary: A US bankruptcy judge has approved Google's $10 million purchase of data belonging to the defunct Spirit Airlines. Google agreed to protections for the data and plans to use it in AI projects.

headline: Report ranks Africa as most-attacked region, driven by a surge in attacks on Nigeria
summary: A threat report ranks Africa as the most-attacked region again. Nigeria faced more than twice as many cyber threats as the previous year, according to the report. Angola and Kenya are also among the five most-attacked countries worldwide.

headline: Strike Graph launches agentic AI tool for automated compliance evidence collection
summary: Strike Graph has released Integration AI, an agentic tool that pulls compliance evidence from existing systems through their APIs. The vendor says it maps that evidence to more than 30 frameworks without duplicate work.

headline: nbdkit qcow2dec filter heap over-read via crafted ZSTD-compressed QCOW2 image (CVE-2026-130888)
summary: The qcow2dec filter in nbdkit sets the wrong ZSTD input buffer size. A crafted QCOW2 image can therefore cause a heap over-read, which may crash the service and could expose heap memory. The source index does not confirm whether Amazon Linux is affected or patched.

headline: rsyslog imuxsock PRI parsing hardening assigned CVE-2026-129831
summary: A source patch limits imuxsock PRI digit parsing to three digits. CVE-2026-129831 covers this change. The maintainers call it robustness hardening and did not find a separate security impact. It was disclosed together with a related out-of-bounds write advisory. Amazon Linux affected status and patch availability have not been confirmed.

headline: rsyslog option.json templates can emit malformed JSON for certain field values (CVE-2026-129839)
summary: rsyslog templates that use option.json can produce malformed JSON when a field value contains only quotes or only backslashes. This could break or confuse systems that ingest the logs downstream. The index does not confirm whether Amazon Linux is affected or patched.

headline: SANS ISC diary proposes Git-based workflow with human review for AI-assisted honeypot analysis
summary: A SANS ISC guest diary proposes managing honeypot analysis like code. It uses Git, pull requests and a mandatory human approval step before accepting AI-generated output. The source summary gives no further detail.

headline: Palo Alto Networks to acquire AI startup Applied Compute in $4.5B all-stock deal
summary: Palo Alto Networks plans to buy Applied Compute in an all-stock deal valued at $4.5 billion, subject to adjustments. Applied Compute's platform handles post-training and inference for open-weight AI models in public and sovereign clouds. The vendor says the deal will help enterprises adopt AI securely.

headline: Bitwarden adds native passkey integration for Windows and macOS
summary: Bitwarden now lets users unlock their vaults with passkeys verified through Windows Hello or Touch ID. Windows 11 and macOS can also recognize Bitwarden as a passkey provider, so passkeys created through the OS stay stored in the Bitwarden vault.

headline: Innokas VC150 vital signs monitor: CISA updates advisory on XSS and HL7 injection flaws
summary: CISA has updated its medical advisory for the Innokas VC150 vital signs monitor. A stored XSS flaw and an HL7 v2.x injection flaw via a connected barcode reader could alter downstream communications or disable some device features. Version 1.7.15b fixes both.

headline: libXfont2 before 2.0.10 out-of-bounds read lets local client crash X server (CVE-2026-109920)
summary: An uninitialized variable in libXfont2's FreeType backend leads to an out-of-bounds read. A local client with low privileges can crash the X server by making it load a font from a path the client controls. The flaw is fixed in version 2.0.10, but the index does not say whether Amazon Linux is affected.

headline: Microsoft tests Edge Lockdown Mode that disables WebGL and WebGPU APIs
summary: Microsoft is building a new Lockdown Mode for Edge. It shrinks the browser's attack surface by turning off the WebGL, WebGL2 and WebGPU graphics APIs. The feature is still in testing.

headline: Malwarebytes tracks GTA 6 launch scams targeting Google credentials and crypto wallets
summary: Malwarebytes researchers found scams using the GTA 6 launch as bait, including fake giveaways that ask for Google passwords. Other lures sell game keys that may never arrive, push players to connect crypto wallets, or offer a phone app that mostly serves ads. The targets are mainly consumers.

headline: Rubrik launches configuration rollback tool for Microsoft 365
summary: Rubrik announced Configuration Resilience, a product that protects Microsoft 365, Purview and Defender settings. It can undo unauthorized configuration changes in a single action.

headline: StepSecurity raises $20 million for software supply-chain security platform
summary: StepSecurity has raised $20 million. The company says the money will speed up development and distribution of its supply-chain protection platform.

headline: Guidance on telling a cyberattack apart from an ordinary IT outage
summary: This explainer warns against assuming that every large outage is a cyberattack. It covers how to tell malicious incidents from ordinary failures.

headline: Microsoft launches a new security check for Windows 11 PCs
summary: Microsoft has released a new check that reports whether a Windows 11 system meets certain security requirements. The source excerpt does not say which requirements it checks.

headline: curl maintainer questions whether AI-agent Rust rewrites of curl can keep pace with upstream fixes
summary: curl maintainer Daniel Stenberg says AI-generated Rust ports of curl miss hundreds of bugfixes and several vulnerability fixes made upstream while the ports were being produced. He questions whether such clones can keep up with maintenance.

headline: Vero Security raises $11 million for AI security engineering platform
summary: Startup Vero Security has raised $11 million in funding for a platform it describes as AI security engineering. The announcement contains no threat or vulnerability information.

headline: BackBox Linux 10 penetration testing distribution released with Ubuntu 26.04 base
summary: The BackBox community project has released version 10 of its penetration testing distribution. It is based on Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, adds new tools and changes anonymous mode so that DNS goes through Tor and IPv6 is blocked.

headline: llm-gemini 0.38 adds support for Google's new Gemini 4 Neon model
summary: Simon Willison released llm-gemini 0.38 to support Google's newly announced Gemini 4 Neon model. The post covers confusing pricing across the Gemini 4 lineup and informal output comparisons between models. It has no security content.

headline: SANS ISC Stormcast podcast for November 17, 2026
summary: SANS ISC published its daily Stormcast podcast episode. The source gives no content details.

headline: datasette-arrows plugin adds Apache Arrow streaming export to Datasette
summary: A new Datasette plugin adds a streaming export option in the Apache Arrow format. It uses the plugin hook for streaming exports added in Datasette 1.0a43. The release has no security content.
